title: Canary rollout scratchpad - Liam Rivera
content:
Objective:
- Validate redwood-serving runtime changes for model routing & KV-cache improvements (PR #1023) under production-like traffic before full rollout.

Scope:
- Canary traffic: 1% of production requests for 24 hours, then evaluate for 48h at 5% if stable.
- Regions: us-west1 primary; canary instances only in us-west1 for this iteration.
- Models: default text-generation routes only (no embeddings or long-context routes).

Versions / pinning notes:
- New runtime image: runtime-redwood:v2024-11-1 (contains PR #1023 kernel selection).
- Current stable image: runtime-redwood:v2024-10-12.
- Canary config: route-level pinning via rollout policy: "canary_percent: 1, match: route==/v1/generate" + fallback to stable if error>threshold.
- If we need to rollback: pin all traffic to v2024-10-12 via Console -> Deployments -> Pin version (or kubectl apply canary-rollout=0).

Checklist (pre-rollout):
- [ ] Confirm smoke tests passing on runtime-redwood:v2024-11-1 in staging (tag: smoke/2024-11-07) - Maya
- [ ] Canary infra: reserve 2x smaller instance pool in us-west1, ensure autoscaler cooldown set to 5m - Isaac
- [ ] Update Nginx routing and traffic-split policy in config repo (INF-3124) - PR merged
- [ ] Create alerting rules for canary-specific metrics (below) - Samir
- [ ] Post announcement in #canary-rollouts + on-call page - Olivia

Canary run plan (day-by-day):
- T=0 (rollout start): divert 1% traffic to runtime-redwood:v2024-11-1.
  - Run quick canary smoke: 100 synthetic requests with 95th latency threshold 220ms.
  - Verify 200 OK ratio > 99% for synths.
- T+1h: Check primary dashboards and logs. If error_rate>0.5% or 95p latency regresses by >30% -> immediate rollback.
- T+24h: If stable, increase to 5% for next 48h.
- T+72h: Post-mortem evaluation. If no regressions, schedule ramp to 25% then 100% over 48-72h with ops approval.

Key metrics and thresholds (canary-specific):
- 5xx rate (per-route): alert if >0.5% absolute increase vs baseline or >0.8% total.
- Latency p95: alert if > +30% vs baseline p95 or >500ms absolute for text generation.
- Token cost per 1k: monitor for +10% delta (unexpected batching/kv changes).
- Model quality regressions: run eval suite (regression-set-v3) hourly; block if quality drop >2% on critical prompts.
- Error budget: maintain <0.25% SLA burn in canary pool.

Dashboards to watch (Console names):
- ops/canary/latency-by-model
- ops/canary/errors-and-5xx
- ops/canary/cost-per-token
- evals/canary/regressions

Automated hooks + runbooks:
- If alert fires (5xx or latency) -> PagerDuty runbook 'Canary runtime regression' (link in Confluence).
- Rolling rollback steps (manual):
  1) Pin all routes to runtime-redwood:v2024-10-12 in Console.
  2) Scale canary pool down to 0% via autoscaling policy.
  3) Re-run smoke tests on stable; notify stakeholders.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Do we need a separate KV-cache warmup step for canary instances? (Maya to prototype warmup script)
- Should we enable prefix caching on canary? Risk: reduces cold-start errors but may hide regressions in cache logic. Proposal: disabled for first 24h.
- Telemetry gap: need per-model token breakdown in traces (INF-3129) - file follow-up ticket.

Post-rollout evaluation checklist:
- [ ] No persistent 5xx or p95 regressions at 5% over 72h.
- [ ] Eval suite shows <1% drift on critical prompts.
- [ ] Cost per token within +5% of baseline.
- [ ] Confirm logs show no increase in OOMs or kernel-fallbacks.
- [ ] Product sign-off (CS/PM) on quality.

Notes to self / conversational fragments:
- If we see intermittent kernel fallback logs: could be quantization mismatch on new kernel selection; check PR #1023 notes.
- Keep canary in single AZ to reduce cross-AZ variables.
- Remember to run the full canary after merging the autoscaler cooldown fix (if Isaac's change lands).

History / related runs:
- Last canary (2024-09): rolled runtime v2024-09-15 -> minor latency uptick; rolled back within 8h. Root cause: batching edge-case.
- Learnings: need faster rollback path and more granular metrics (route-level).

Appendix: useful commands/snippets
- Pin version via API: curl -X POST https://console.redwood.ai/api/v1/deployments/pin -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' -d '{"route":"/v1/generate","image":"runtime-redwood:v2024-10-12"}'
- Check canary logs: rl logs --env=prod --service=runtime --filter='image:v2024-11-1' --since=1h
- Run eval locally: python tools/eval_runner.py --suite regression-set-v3 --target http://canary-proxy:8080/v1/generate

-- LR
